metadata.title: Body recomposition in adults: mechanisms, modulators, and practical algorithms for simultaneous skeletal muscle mass gain and fat mass loss.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Body recomposition is the concurrent increase in fat-free mass (FFM) or skeletal muscle mass and decrease in fat mass (FM) within the same intervention period. Although hypertrophy is commonly pursued in energy surplus and FM loss in energy deficit, controlled trials indicate that recomposition can occur when progressive resistance training (PRT), adequate protein intake, and an appropriate energy prescription are combined. METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of randomised trials, meta-analyses, and selected mechanistic studies in adults, with emphasis on FFM, FM, strength, and performance outcomes. Device heterogeneity was considered when interpreting evidence, with greatest weight placed on four-compartment and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) outcomes. RESULTS: PRT combined with higher protein intake, typically ~1.6-2.4 g/kg/day and higher relative intakes during energy restriction or leanness, is the most consistent strategy for recomposition. Effects are largest in untrained individuals and those with higher adiposity, smaller in trained or lean athletes, and still feasible in older adults when anabolic resistance is addressed with supervised PRT and sufficient protein. Moderate deficits, carbohydrate allocation around key sessions, sleep, and recovery support FFM retention or accretion while facilitating FM loss. Practical applications: Programmes should pair progressive overload with protein-centred diets, modest energy deficits, and periodic monitoring of body composition and performance. CONCLUSIONS: Body recomposition is feasible but context-dependent; expected changes are generally modest in trained or lean populations and require individualised adjustment.

metadata.title: Neuromuscular performance, physiological recovery, and maturation-referenced reference values in youth athletes: A cross-sectional study.
metadata.abstract: This cross-sectional study characterized neuromuscular performance and acute physiological responses across age, sex, and biological maturation in 140 youth athletes (74 boys, 66 girls; 10-16 years), and described maturation-stratified distributions of two field measures. Participants completed 30-m sprint, countermovement jump (CMJ), standing long jump (SLJ), and handgrip testing; post-sprint heart-rate recovery (HRrec-30s) and a testing-battery perceived-exertion index (PEI) served as co-primary physiological/perceptual outcomes; maturity offset (Mirwald method) classified Pre-, Circa-, and Post-PHV subgroups; allometric scaling was used to account for body size; and a Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied across a pre-specified family of 58 pairwise comparisons and correlations (Tables 2-6). Boys outperformed girls across all neuromuscular tests (d = 0.63-0.76), whereas HRrec-30s and the perceived-exertion index did not differ significantly by sex. HRrec-30s was more strongly associated with maturity offset than with chronological age (r = 0.52 vs 0.46; η²p for maturation vs age groups 0.43 vs 0.39). Mean HRrec-30s was 27.8 ± 6.2 bpm in the Pre-PHV group and 45.3 ± 8.8 bpm in the Post-PHV group (p < 0.001, FDR-corrected). The perceived-exertion index was lower in more mature groups (7.5 ± 1.2 vs 6.3 ± 1.1). Sex and maturation differences in jump and strength performance remained after allometric scaling, although they were smaller. Maturation-stratified distributions reported here are preliminary and descriptive and are not decision thresholds; prospective, criterion-validated research is needed before they can be recommended for individual athlete monitoring or training-load decision-making.

metadata.title: Chlorella intake combined with short-term high-intensity intermittent training further enhances exercise performance in female lacrosse players: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover trial.
metadata.abstract: Lacrosse is a fast-paced field sport that requires aerobic, anaerobic, and sprint performance. Chronic Chlorella intake combined with high-intensity intermittent training (HIIT) enhances aerobic, anaerobic, and sprint performance in untrained young adults. This study aimed to clarify the effects of combining Chlorella intake with short-term HIIT on aerobic, anaerobic, and sprint performance in female lacrosse players. In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial, twelve female collegiate lacrosse players were enrolled, ten participants completed 3 weeks of HIIT, comprising 7 bouts of running at full speed with a 10-second rest between each bout, 5 days/week. They were orally administered Chlorella (CH) or a placebo (PL) for 3-week in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover design with a 5-week washout period. This study measured the 20-meter shuttle run test (20m SRT) and estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max) as indices of aerobic performance, 50-meter sprint time as an index of sprint performance, and the 30-second Wingate test as an index of anaerobic performance. No significant differences by trial or time point were observed in aerobic (20m SRT and VO2max) or anaerobic performance (Wingate test), including 50-meter sprint time. However, improvements were observed in the HIIT + CH trial for most exercise performance outcomes (P < 0.05), but not in the HIIT + PL trial. These exploratory results suggest that CH intake may improve short-term HIIT-induced changes in exercise performance in female lacrosse players, although the small sample size and short intervention period warrant cautious interpretation.

metadata.title: Pelvic floor knowledge and unhealthy habits related in female athletes: a cross-sectional study.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe pelvic floor (PF)-related knowledge and unhealthy habits among female athletes, and to examine their associations with PF dysfunction (PFD) symptoms, sports characteristics, academic level and help seeking attitudes. METHODS: A total of 538 female athletes (36.7 ± 11.3 years) completed an anonymous online questionnaire covering age, academic level, sports experience, unhealthy PF-related habits, PFD symptoms, professional healthcare-seeking attitude and knowledge about urinary incontinence (UI), anorectal incontinence (ARI), pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and female sexual dysfunction (FSD). Adequate knowledge was considered as ≥70% correct responses. RESULTS: Female athletes demonstrated adequate knowledge regarding UI, ARI and POP, but insufficient knowledge about FSD (52.6%). Several PFD symptoms were associated with lower knowledge levels and a higher number of unhealthy habits compared with athletes without these symptoms (p<0.05). Younger athletes showed lower knowledge about ARI (p=0.033) and POP (p=0.003), while older athletes showed lower knowledge about FSD (p<0.001). Athletes who rejected professional healthcare showed lower knowledge across all PFD domains (p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Female athletes reporting symptoms suggestive of PFD showed lower levels of knowledge and a higher number of unhealthy PF habits compared with those without symptoms. Although athletes generally demonstrated an appropriate level of knowledge regarding PFD, important gaps were observed in the FSD domain and in unhealthy toileting and sport-related habits, particularly among athletes without university studies. Differences in knowledge were also observed according to age and healthcare-seeking attitudes, highlighting areas that may be considered in future educational initiatives.

metadata.title: Different osteoarthritis progression rates within early-stage knee osteoarthritis: a retrospective cohort study using machine learning cluster analysis from the osteoarthritis initiative database.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous disease with varying progression rates among patients within the same severity grade. This study aimed to identify clinically interpretable radiographic phenotypes among knees with baseline Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grade 2 osteoarthritis and to compare their 4-year radiographic progression patterns using baseline radiographic features, lifetime exercise patterns, and demographic characteristics. METHODS: Data of patients with baseline KL grade 2 from the Osteoarthritis Initiative database were retrieved. Unsupervised clustering was performed using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) for dimensionality reduction, followed by hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN) to identify distinct subgroups. The proportion of knees progressing to KL grade ≥ 3 within 4 years was compared between subgroups, followed by a survival analysis until knee replacement or progression to KL grade 4. RESULTS: A total of 1997 knees with a mean follow-up of 103.3 months (maximum, 108 months) were included. A total of seven subgroups were identified and classified into accelerated osteoarthritis progression (AOP) group and slow osteoarthritis progression (SOP) group according to whether their 4-year KL grade progression proportions were above or below the training-set average. In a supportive long-term survival analysis, the AOP group also showed significantly earlier progression to knee replacement or KL grade 4 than the SOP group (training set, P < 0.001; test set, P = 0.049), although the absolute difference in mean survival time was modest (8.3 versus 8.5 years in the training set; 8.4 versus 8.6 years in the test set). The AOP group was characterized mainly by lateral joint space narrowing (JSN) and medial JSN with subchondral sclerosis, whereas the SOP group was characterized by medial JSN without subchondral sclerosis, osteophyte-dominant patterns without JSN, or chondrocalcinosis-dominant patterns; these differences were statistically significant across clusters. CONCLUSIONS: Within baseline KL grade 2 knees, clinically interpretable radiographic phenotypes, including lateral JSN, medial JSN with subchondral sclerosis, osteophyte-dominant changes without JSN, and chondrocalcinosis-dominant patterns, were associated with different 4-year KL grade progression rates. These findings support viewing KL grade 2 knee OA as a heterogeneous radiographic stage that may be further stratified into phenotype-based subgroups with different short-term radiographic prognoses.

metadata.title: Prevalence and associated factors of depression, anxiety, and stress among university athletes in Bangladesh.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: University athletes face substantial academic, physical, and psychosocial pressures that may heighten vulnerability to psychological distress, despite the perceived mental health benefits of sports participation. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress among university athletes in Bangladesh and to examine how these conditions are associated with lifestyle and sociodemographic factors. METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from March to September 2025 among 249 university athletes aged 18-26 years at six randomly selected universities in Bangladesh. Data were collected online and in person. Psychological distress was assessed with the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), and health-promoting lifestyle behaviors were evaluated with the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP-II). Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Spearman's correlations, and binary logistic regression analyses were conducted. RESULTS: The prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress was 42.6%, 42.6%, and 43.8%, respectively. Depression, anxiety, and stress were significantly associated with relationship status, fatigue, socioeconomic status, smoking, sleep duration, sports participation frequency, and satisfaction with sports (all p < 0.05). Participants with depression, anxiety, and stress had significantly lower scores across all HPLP-II domains (all p < 0.01). Higher physical activity was independently associated with lower odds of depression (OR = 0.462, 95% CI: 0.286-0.746), anxiety (OR = 0.756, 95% CI: 0.677-0.845), and stress (OR = 0.773, 95% CI: 0.677-0.882). Better stress management and stronger interpersonal relationships were also significantly associated, whereas other factors were not. CONCLUSIONS: Depression, anxiety, and stress were highly prevalent among university athletes in Bangladesh and strongly associated with modifiable lifestyle factors. These findings support integrated, athlete-centered mental health strategies emphasizing physical activity, stress management, and psychosocial support. However, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and determination of the directionality of these associations. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

metadata.title: Residual Postural-Control Differences After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: Dual-Task Postural Control and Associations with Time Since Return to Sport.
metadata.abstract: Background/Objectives: Residual sensorimotor deficits may persist after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), even after clearance for unrestricted sport. This study compared unilateral postural control between individuals after ACLR and healthy controls under visual deprivation and cognitive dual-task conditions and examined associations between dual-task cost and time since reconstruction and return to activity. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 35 physically active adults 9-24 months after primary unilateral ACLR and 35 age-, sex-, body mass index-, and activity-matched controls. Force-platform posturography measured center-of-pressure (COP) path length, ellipse area, and mean velocity during unilateral stance with eyes open, eyes closed, and concurrent serial subtraction. COP path-length dual-task cost (DTC) was compared between groups and limbs. Correlation and multiple linear regression analyses examined associations with postoperative and return-to-activity duration. Results: Eyes-closed COP path length was greater in reconstructed limbs than in control reference limbs (720.00 ± 118.00 versus 552.00 ± 92.00 mm; p < 0.001). Reconstructed-limb DTC exceeded control reference-limb DTC (17.45 ± 10.20% versus 6.97 ± 6.80%; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.21) and contralateral-limb DTC (11.00 ± 8.40%; p < 0.001). Longer time since ACLR (r = -0.38; p = 0.024) and return to unrestricted activity (r = -0.44; p = 0.008) were associated with lower DTC. Both associations remained significant in a two-predictor regression model (adjusted R2 = 0.20). Conclusions: Postural-control differences persisted after ACLR despite clearance for unrestricted activity and were more evident under visual deprivation and cognitive loading. These cross-sectional associations support further investigation of dual-task posturography in postoperative assessment. The clinical significance and predictive value of these static posturographic measures for return-to-sport readiness and subsequent injury risk remain to be established.

metadata.title: Smartphone Accelerometer Assessment of HRV: Concurrent Agreement of the KubiosHRV App.
metadata.abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) is widely used to monitor athlete recovery and adaptation. Recent technological advances have enabled HRV assessment through smartphone applications without the need for external devices. This study aimed to assess the concurrent agreement between the accelerometer-based HRV measurement feature of the KubiosHRV app and the Polar H10 in supine, seated, and standing positions. A total of 52 participants (30 males and 22 females) across performance tiers 0-4 completed a 2 min resting recording, with the first minute discarded and the second minute analysed in each position. HRV was measured simultaneously using a Polar H10 chest strap and the accelerometer-based feature of the KubiosHRV app on an iPhone 14. The analysed variables included Mean RR, RMSSD, SDNN, LF power, HF power, SD1, and SD2. Data were automatically processed by the KubiosHRV app and manually extracted into a database. Results showed excellent intraclass correlation coefficients (≥0.985) and small magnitudes of error for time-domains and non-linear variables in the three analysed positions with the reference criterion. Frequency-domain variables showed larger error estimates. Bland-Altman analysis showed no evidence of proportional bias across the measurement range (p > 0.05). These findings suggest that, during 1 min recordings, the accelerometer-based feature of the KubiosHRV app showed strong concurrent agreement with the Polar H10 for time-domain variables and acceptable agreement for selected non-linear variables across positions. Therefore, it may represent a practical alternative for routine monitoring of these HRV metrics when external hardware is unavailable.

metadata.title: Time Course of Lipid Peroxidation, Antioxidant Markers and C-Reactive Protein Following Simulated Soccer Match-Play: A 72-h Study in Semi-Professional Players.
metadata.abstract: Background/Objectives: Soccer match-play triggers muscle damage and a marked increase in reactive oxygen species production, but early and late lipid peroxidation products have rarely been tracked together with non-enzymatic antioxidants and C-reactive protein in the same players over a full 72-h window. This study characterized the recovery kinetics of oxidative damage markers (conjugated dienes, malondialdehyde) and antioxidant/defense markers (uric acid, bilirubin, reduced glutathione, gamma-glutamyl transferase), together with C-reactive protein, and explored the relationships between these markers' recovery responses. Methods: Twelve semi-professional male soccer players completed the Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). Venous blood samples were collected at Baseline, 0 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h post-LIST. Repeated-measures ANOVA or the Friedman test was applied depending on normality, with Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons against Baseline and exploratory Spearman correlations. Results: Uric acid and reduced glutathione peaked at 0 h and no longer differed significantly from baseline from 24 h and 48 h onward, respectively. CRP increased significantly at 24 h, whereas bilirubin showed only a non-significant 24-h peak. Conjugated dienes remained significantly elevated at every time point up to 72 h, whereas malondialdehyde differed significantly from baseline only at 0 h. In exploratory analyses not corrected for multiple testing, uric acid correlated with bilirubin and, on an area-under-the-curve basis, with C-reactive protein, and conjugated dienes correlated with malondialdehyde. Conclusions: The uric acid and reduced glutathione responses and the C-reactive protein response resolved within 24 to 48 h, whereas conjugated dienes remained elevated up to 72 h. These findings indicate prolonged alterations in selected circulating biomarkers rather than direct evidence of persistent muscle oxidative damage or incomplete functional recovery, and their relevance to congested fixture scheduling warrants investigation alongside performance outcomes.

metadata.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Late European away fixtures can disrupt sleep, but the influence of immediate return versus overnight stay, and whether responses differ by match participation, remains unclear. HYPOTHESIS: Postmatch travel strategy would influence sleep quality and duration across the prematch, match, and subsequent nights, with responses moderated by match participation. STUDY DESIGN: Observational repeated-measures field study. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3. METHODS: A total of 19 outfield English Premier League players were monitored across 10 European away fixtures (5 immediate return and 5 overnight stay). Self-reported sleep quality (1 to 7) and sleep duration were recorded on the prematch, match, and subsequent nights. Fixed-effects models examined condition, time, and match participation, with standard errors clustered by player. RESULTS: Sleep quality was lower than prematch baseline on the match and subsequent nights (both β = -0.62 arbitrary units [AU]; P < 0.01; g = -0.63). After overnight stay, sleep quality improved from the match to the subsequent night in players who participated and those who did not (β = 0.69 and 0.63 AU; 95% CIs, 0.37-0.90 and 0.47-0.91; P < 0.01), whereas no change occurred after immediate return. Across participation groups, sleep duration was lower after overnight stay than immediate return on the match night (β = -1.94 hours; P < 0.01; g = -1.26) and subsequent night (β = -1.02 hours; P = 0.02; g = -0.67). However, after overnight stay, sleep duration increased between these nights by 1.45 hours in participants and 1.43 hours in nonparticipants (P < 0.01), with no significant change after immediate return. Participation moderated sleep duration on both postfixture nights (β = 1.27 and 1.64 hours; P ≤ 0.04; g = 0.82 and 1.07). CONCLUSION: Neither travel strategy was uniformly superior. Overnight stay was associated with poorer absolute sleep duration but a clearer next-night rebound in sleep quality and duration. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Postmatch travel should be planned case by case, considering itinerary, next-day demands, and individual match exposure rather than applying a single team-wide policy.

metadata.title: Enhancing Sleep in NCAA Division I Athletes: A Study of Sleep Extension Feasibility.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sleep extension has been shown to improve varied aspects of athletic performance in collegiate athletes. Such studies have been conducted in small cohorts in controlled settings utilizing obsolete monitoring technology. The feasibility of sleep extension has not been evaluated in a broader cohort of collegiate athletes with modern monitoring technology. HYPOTHESIS: Sleep extension may not be feasible in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I athletes. STUDY DESIGN: Crossover study. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3. METHODS: Baseline sleep data were collected from NCAA Division I athletes (women's soccer, men's soccer, baseball, and football) during a 2-week period. Subjects were then instructed to extend their total sleep time to 10 hours per night for 2 weeks. All sleep baseline and extension data were collected in the offseason, remote from school examinations. WHOOP bands recorded all sleep metrics. Data were analyzed using paired-samples t tests and Wilcoxon signed rank tests. RESULTS: A total of 50 subjects (14 female, 36 male) participated. The study compared total sleep time (hours) and sleep consistency (percent) - the stability of sleep-wake schedule over time, between baseline and sleep extension phases. Sample size varied for both metrics, ranging from 46 to 49 participants, respectively. There was a statistically significant increase in sleep consistency during the sleep extension phase (baseline, 60.09 ± 12.6%; extension, 64.42 ± 12.4%; P = 0.02). However, total sleep time showed no significant difference between the 2 phases (baseline, 7.63 ± 0.88 hours; extension, 7.51 ± 0.88 hours; P = 0.27). CONCLUSION: Extension efforts improved sleep consistency but did not significantly impact total sleep time suggesting that a sleep extension intervention can enhance sleep consistency in NCAA Division I athletes but does not significantly impact total sleep time. Sleep extension may be challenging for collegiate athletes given the time-intensive demands of both academics and sports. While sleep extension may be feasible in professional sports, it does not appear to be so in the college setting. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: While the sleep extension intervention improved sleep consistency, it did not improve total sleep time, questioning the feasibility of sleep extension in collegiate sports.

metadata.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
metadata.abstract: Sebastian-Rico, JM, Muñoz-Fernández, MJ, Martínez-Aranda, LM, Calvo-Lluch, Á, and Ortega-Becerra, M. Effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training in women soccer players and its relationship with quality of life and pelvic floor muscle strength: a randomized controlled pilot study. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study investigated the effects of a 6-week pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) program on muscle strength, function, and the prevalence of related dysfunctions in professional female soccer players using a randomized controlled pilot study design. Twenty nulliparous professional soccer players from the Spanish professional league (2024-2025 season) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 8). Assessments included anthropometric data, validated questionnaires (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form and Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), clinical interviews, and physical examination using the PERFECT method and manometry. The intervention consisted of a 6-week supervised PFMT program (4 sessions/week, 30 minutes each) progressed through 4 phases: education, proprioception, strengthening, and functional integration. Results showed significant group × time interactions for pelvic floor self-efficacy (Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), with scores in the PFMT group increasing by 48.8 and 59.6% (p < 0.05), representing large between-group effect sizes (d = 0.91-1.26). Pelvic floor muscle performance increased by 122.4% in the intervention group (d = 1.25), whereas no meaningful changes were observed in the control group. No adverse events were reported. In conclusion, a 6-week supervised PFMT program is an effective and safe intervention for professional female soccer players, significantly improving muscle function and self-efficacy. These findings support the integration of PFMT for both therapeutic and preventive purposes in elite, high-impact sports environments.

metadata.title: Remotely Supervised Exercise Training is Associated With Partial Attenuation of Detraining-Related Changes in National-Level Adolescent Water Polo Athletes.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to examine changes in body composition and physical performance associated with a home-based exercise training program in national-level adolescent water polo athletes during the first COVID-19 lockdown. METHOD: Forty-one athletes participated in a 7-week home-based exercise program, with pretraining and posttraining assessments of body composition, aerobic capacity (V˙O2max), repeated sprint ability, isometric trunk strength, and throwing speed. RESULTS: Significant improvements were ob in throwing speed for both genders, with males increasing from an average of 8.09 (0.96) to 10.48 (1.31) m/s and females increasing from 6.30 (0.74) to 7.16 (0.87) m/s. Adolescent females experienced significant increases in body mass by 2.81 kg (95% CI, 2.05-3.57; P < .001) and fat percentage by 2.13% (95% CI, 1.28-2.97; P < .001), leading to a decrease in relative V˙O2max by 3.01 mL/kg/min (95% CI, -5.79 to -0.23; P = .035). No significant change was found in posttraining absolute V˙O2max. Among males, repeated sprint ability showed a mixed response, with improved best sprint performance but an increased fatigue index, whereas no significant changes were observed in females. CONCLUSION: A home-based exercise training program demonstrated potential for partially mitigating detraining-related changes in national-level adolescent water polo athletes, particularly by maintaining or improving selected aspects of physical performance.

metadata.title: Nationwide Trends, Regional Variation and Seasonality of Surgically Treated Achilles Tendon Rupture in Japan: An Analysis of Descriptive Epidemiological Study.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Achilles tendon rupture (ATR) is a common foot and ankle injury among physically active adults. Nationwide evidence on long-term trends, regional variation, seasonality and COVID-19-related changes in Japan is limited. We characterised the surgical burden of ATR using a national administrative database. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide descriptive epidemiological study using aggregated data from the National Database of Health Insurance Claims and Specific Health Checkups (NDB) Open Data for fiscal years (FY) 2014-2022. Temporal trends, prefectural variation, seasonal patterns and pandemic-associated changes were examined using counts, population-based rates and quasi-Poisson regression. RESULTS: During FY2014-2019, approximately 11,200 surgeries were performed annually (8.8 per 100,000 person). In FY2020, incidence declined to 5.9 per 100,000 (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.67), with greater reductions among adults aged 30-59 (61%-64% of baseline) and, after age adjustment, among women (IRR 0.61 vs. 0.71 in men; interaction p = 0.039). Incidence partially recovered in FY2021-2022 (7.6 per 100,000; IRR 0.86). Incidence varied across the 47 prefectures (pre-COVID range: 5.0-16.7 per 100,000), and all declined in FY2020 (mean ratio 0.69). Monthly counts peaked in spring-early summer and were higher in spring than in winter (p = 0.018). CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of surgically treated ATR in Japan was stable before the COVID-19 pandemic, declined markedly in FY2020 and partially recovered thereafter, with the largest reductions among working-age adults and women. Regional variation and seasonality were preserved. These findings can inform surgical and rehabilitation service planning.

metadata.title: Sleep Management in Paralympic Sports: Knowledge, Monitoring Practices, and Perceived Barriers among Coaches and Healthcare Staff.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Coaches and healthcare staff play a crucial role in disseminating knowledge about the importance of sleep to develop a precise balance between recovery and the demands imposed by sports training. OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge on sleep, jet lag, and sleep hygiene (SH) among coaches and healthcare staff in Paralympic sports; 2) to identify whether the sleep of Paralympic athletes is monitored, and which instruments are commonly used; and 3) to identify the main barriers faced in sleep management. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present cross-sectional study was conducted with 60 coaches and healthcare staff who work in the preparation of elite Paralympic athletes. The participants filled out the Sleep Beliefs Scale and a structured questionnaire before traveling to the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games. RESULTS: Coaches and healthcare staff understand the importance of sleep for sports performance and recovery, but only 56% monitored their sleep. The most commonly used methods were subjective. Lack of adherence and commitment among Paralympic athletes (27%) and lack of training (19%) were the main barriers to sleep management. CONCLUSION: Coaches and healthcare staff are aware of the importance of sleep; however, educational programs are needed to improve the training of coaching and healthcare staff for efficient sleep management and to raise awareness among Paralympic athletes about the importance of sleep.

metadata.title: Statistical Parametric Mapping reveals sex-specific, phase-dependent differences in bilateral three-dimensional ground reaction force during Wushu Changbing PiJi in high-level athletes.
metadata.abstract: PiJi is a core attacking technique in Wushu Changbing competition, but continuous waveform evidence remains limited regarding the sex-specific phase characteristics of bilateral 3D ground reaction force (GRF) during PiJi performed with maximal voluntary effort (MVE). This study aimed to compare continuous changes in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral GRF between high-level male and female athletes during PiJi performed with MVE. In this cross-sectional, laboratory-based observational study, 44 right-hand-dominant athletes, including 22 male athletes and 22 female athletes, performed PiJi with MVE, yielding 616 valid trials. Bilateral 3D GRF was recorded using two force plates. Each trial was time-normalized and linearly interpolated to 143 equally spaced nodes, and within-participant mean waveforms were calculated before between-group differences were analyzed using statistical parametric mapping. Primary analyses used random-field-theory inference, with sensitivity examined using 5,000 permutation tests. After Bonferroni correction, phase-specific sex differences were detected in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral 3D GRF. Scalar localization showed that male athletes had higher trailing-foot Fy during the middle phase (33.98%-47.04%) and higher trailing-foot Fx (62.41%-71.99%) and net bilateral Fx (54.18%-70.41%) during the middle-to-late phase; female athletes showed only a brief period of higher trailing-foot vertical Fz during the middle phase (42.11%-44.61%). Although lead-foot 3D GRF differed overall, no confirmatory difference was localized to any single scalar component. These findings indicate that sex-related GRF differences in high-level PiJi were concentrated mainly in specific horizontal-plane phases of trailing-foot and net bilateral force, whereas the lead-foot difference was identified only at the overall 3D GRF level. These results provide kinetic evidence for phase-specific assessment of PiJi technique and suggest that training monitoring and mechanistic research should consider foot, direction, and movement phase rather than relying only on peak force or discrete variables. Future studies integrating multimodal measures and sport-specific performance may further clarify the functional significance of bilateral force-generation patterns.

metadata.title: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
metadata.abstract: This study explores the feasibility of implementing and evaluating a community-based physical activity programme for individuals with Long Covid in Hertfordshire, UK. Long Covid presents unique challenges including fluctuating symptoms, post-exertional malaise and difficulties with re-engagement following symptom flare-ups. Developed collaboratively by the Herts Sports & Physical Activity Partnership and local NHS Covid Rehabilitation Services, the programme aimed to address these challenges through tailored physical activity opportunities informed by the lived experience of Long Covid. A longitudinal observational design was used to evaluate programme retention, symptom severity, health-related quality of life and physical activity levels among 62 participants over a 12-month period. Data were collected via validated self-report tools including the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, SBQ-LC and VAS pain scale. High initial engagement was observed, with 89% of participants completing the first follow-up survey and 52% remaining engaged through to follow-up 4. While average physical activity minutes remained stable, the proportion of inactive participants declined from 37% to 25%. Statistically significant improvements were observed in self-rated health (EQ-VAS), breathing difficulties, fatigue and brain fog. Weak but significant correlations were found between increased physical activity and reduced symptom severity in several domains, including mobility, self-care and musculoskeletal pain. No significant changes were observed in anxiety or depression, suggesting physical activity alone may not address the full spectrum of Long Covid symptoms. These findings demonstrate that community-based physical activity interventions are feasible for people with Long Covid, though sustained behavioural change and mental health support remain important challenges. This study contributes practical insights for service development while highlighting the need for more rigorous controlled designs and diverse sampling in future research.

metadata.title: Creatine and Beta-Alanine Supplementation for Endurance Athletes: Ergogenic Aids for Reaching the Podium?
metadata.abstract: Endurance sports are characterized mainly by prolonged exercise demands. Although endurance performance is primarily supported by aerobic metabolism, anaerobic energy pathways, buffering capacity, neuromuscular resilience, and the ability to tolerate fatigue during decisive moments of a race are also relevant to competitive success. In this context, creatine and beta-alanine supplementation are two ergogenic strategies purported to enhance endurance performance. This review critically examines the physiological rationale and current evidence regarding creatine supplementation, beta-alanine supplementation, and their cosupplementation in endurance sports. The available literature suggests that beta-alanine may improve performance in exercise tasks performed in the aerobic-anaerobic transition zone, through increased skeletal muscle carnosine content and enhanced intracellular buffering capacity. Creatine supplementation may support endurance performance by increasing phosphocreatine availability, improving glycogen resynthesis and buffering capacity, attenuating exercise-induced inflammation and muscle damage, preserving fast-twitch muscle characteristics, and enhancing repeated sprint ability or late-race power output. However, evidence supporting improvements in classical markers of aerobic performance, such as VO2max, lactate threshold, and time-to-exhaustion, remains inconsistent, and the available evidence has been derived from untrained or recreationally active individuals, limiting direct translation to highly trained endurance athletes. Therefore, the practical relevance of these supplements appears to depend on the athlete's training phase, event characteristics (e.g., weight-bearing or not), competitive goal, and performance level. Creatine and beta-alanine should not be viewed as universal ergogenic aids for endurance athletes, but rather as targeted nutritional strategies that may be particularly useful in race contexts where repeated high-intensity efforts, fatigue resistance, and decisive finishing actions influence performance.

metadata.title: Dysphagia as the Initial Manifestation of Anti-HMGCR Antibody-Positive Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-positive immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels. Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: An 83-year-old man with brief, remote statin exposure presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a three-year history of oropharyngeal dysphagia preceding limb involvement. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated creatine kinase and transaminases. Anti-HMGCR antibodies were positive, and muscle biopsy confirmed necrotizing myopathy. During evaluation for occult malignancy, bilateral pulmonary emboli were incidentally identified. The patient required high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory disease. With aggressive immunosuppressive therapy and rehabilitation, he demonstrated substantial clinical recovery at 6 months. CONCLUSION: This case highlights oropharyngeal dysphagia as an early and, for a prolonged period, isolated manifestation of anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM; here, it preceded the onset of limb weakness by approximately 3 years. It underscores the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation in patients with unexplained oropharyngeal dysfunction, in whom an inflammatory myopathy may otherwise be overlooked for years. Clinicians should maintain awareness of thrombotic risk in inflammatory myopathies, particularly during active disease. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy remain critical to optimize outcomes and prevent irreversible muscle damage.

metadata.title: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders among civil servants attending healthcare facilities in Bangladesh: An observational cross-sectional study.
metadata.abstract: BackgroundWork-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) are a major occupational health concern worldwide, significantly affecting employees' well-being and productivity. Government employees in Bangladesh are particularly vulnerable to WMSDs due to the sedentary or repetitive nature of their work (e.g., prolonged computer use, repetitive typing, and manual mechanical tasks).ObjectiveThis study aimed to determine the clinical distribution, patterns, and associated factors of WMSDs among government employees in Bangladesh and evaluate the subjective impact on workers' productivity and quality of life.MethodsA retrospective descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Employees Hospital in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Participants were recruited using consecutive sampling from government employees attending the Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Department. Descriptive and inferential statistics (Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests via R software) were used to examine the distribution of conditions like low back pain, knee osteoarthritis, cervical spondylosis, frozen shoulder. Productivity and quality of life were assessed through structured clinical interviews, while demographic characteristics, work type, and employment grade were analyzed to identify associated factors.ResultsNonspecific low back pain was the most prevalent condition (27.23%), particularly among retired employees (34.62%) and sedentary workers (26.97%). Knee osteoarthritis (10.81%) and cervical spondylosis (8.97%) were more common among older and dynamic workers. The most commonly affected sites were the lower back (43.73%), knees, shoulders, and neck. Disease patterns varied significantly by age, and government service grade.ConclusionThe high proportion of diagnosed cases among Bangladeshi government employees underscores the need for interventions including ergonomic modifications, regular health assessments, and early screening strategies to reduce WMSD impact and inform public sector health policies.

metadata.title: 18-years Follow-up after Mosaicplasty in Adolescent Athletes with Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Elbow.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty is an established surgical treatment of unstable osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) lesions of the elbow. However, the information on the long-term outcomes is lacking. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the long-term clinical and radiographic results after autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty in the treatment of OCD of the elbow. METHODS: This prospective long-term follow-up study is an extension of previously published data on 10 patients treated with autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty due to advanced, unstable OCD at the capitellum from 2003-2007. Objective and patient-reported outcomes were evaluated including Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), Oxford Elbow Score, Quick-Disability of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (Quick-DASH), Timmerman-Andrews Score, a Subjective Elbow Value, and Range of Motion (ROM). Radiographic signs of osteoarthritis were graded according to the Kellgren-Lawrence classification. RESULTS: At mean 18 years (range 16.0-19.7) five patients were available for follow-up. Mean age at follow-up was 34.4, and all five patients were women. MEPS was a median 100 (range 85-100). Activities of daily life were mildly affected in two patients. Two patients had non-symptomatic osteoarthritis grade 1 and 2. Patients experienced a functioning and near-normal elbow. CONCLUSION: The long-term results after mosaicplasty are encouraging, and we find it reasonable to recommend mosaicplasty as the surgical treatment in this group of female patients with advanced, unstable OCD lesions of the elbow. However, it is of concern that two out of five patients had non-symptomatic early radiographic signs of osteoarthritis at an early age. As this study has an inclusion rate of 50 % of the original cohort, attrition bias must be taken into consideration. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, case series, treatment study.

metadata.title: Adhesive and Antibacterial Bio-Based Hydrogel for Human Voice Recognition and Osteoarthritis Recovery Monitoring.
metadata.abstract: Conductive hydrogels derived from natural polysaccharides hold great promise for next generation wearable electronics owing to their intrinsic biocompatibility, adhesiveness, and tunable mechanical properties. However, realizing amylum-based hydrogels with simultaneously high stretchability, sensitivity, strong adhesion and antibacterial performance remains a significant challenge. Herein, a multifunctional ionic hydrogel, marked as PAPC4 hydrogel, composed of polyacrylamide (PAAm), amylum and phenol-modified chitosan is developed via a one-pot synthesis strategy. The hydrogel exhibits exceptional stretchability (up to 1605%), short response time (16.1 ms), high optical transparency (96%), strong adhesion (43.2 kPa on PVC) and pronounced antibacterial activity. Cytotoxicity assays, live/dead staining, and subcutaneous implantation supported its biocompatibility under the tested conditions, while bacterial assays demonstrated activity against Escherichia coli. As a strain sensor, PAPC4 detected joint movements and throat vibrations during speech. It also recorded differences in knee movement among control, osteoarthritis, and treated osteoarthritis groups in rats. These results support the use of this chitosan-starch composite hydrogel in wearable motion sensing and rehabilitation monitoring.

metadata.title: Lateral meniscus posterior root tears in the anterior cruciate ligament-injured knee: Current concepts.
metadata.abstract: Lateral meniscus posterior root tears (LMPRTs) compromise load transmission and secondary stability in the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)-injured knee and may be missed on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This narrative current-concepts review addresses incidence, risk factors, biomechanics, diagnosis, classification, treatment, and outcomes, while distinguishing root tears from lateral meniscal oblique radial tears (LMORTs). Primary ACL reconstruction (ACLR) cohorts report LMPRT frequencies of 7.1%, 10.0%, and 12.2%; a mixed primary/revision cohort reports 6.6% and selected revision cohorts report 20.5% and 40.7%. These study-specific estimates differ in lesion definition and ascertainment. Contact injury, concomitant medial meniscal pathology, and increased lateral posterior tibial slope are recurring associations. Individual MRI signs have limited sensitivity; combined assessment and arthroscopic inspection and probing support diagnosis. LaPrade et al. describe root-tear morphology, Forkel and Petersen additionally consider meniscofemoral ligament integrity, and LMORT typing describes posterior-horn oblique radial tears. The systems overlap for near-root lesions and are descriptive frameworks rather than validated treatment algorithms. Selected stable lesions may be observed; repairable unstable lesions are generally treated with footprint fixation or side-to-side repair, according to anatomy and tissue quality. Repair with ACLRn is associated with improved patient-reported outcomes and high complete-or-partial healing proportions in selected series. Clinical improvement in ACL graft survivorship has not been demonstrated. Heterogeneous definitions, predominantly lower-level evidence, variable rehabilitation, and limited long-term comparative data, constrain conclusions about cartilage preservation and optimal treatment.

metadata.title: Therapeutic potential of umbilical cord-derived MSCs in arthritis: Insights from preclinical and clinical studies.
metadata.abstract: Among different types of arthritis, osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remain the most common and primary cause of pain and disability worldwide, characterized by progressive joint degeneration and persistent inflammation. Although there have been developments in pharmacology, the available treatment program slows disease progression and provides only symptomatic relief. However, their ability to repair and restore damaged tissue is limited. This highlights the importance of regenerative therapy in actively modulating the immune system while stimulating tissue regeneration. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed, Scopus, Web of science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ChiCTR, focusing on preclinical and clinical studies of umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs) therapy in OA and RA. Recently, UC-MSC have been emerging as a promising therapeutic approach due to their immunomodulatory and regenerative properties. Because they are harvested noninvasively, these cells have greater proliferative capacity and lower immunogenicity than MSCs derived from bone marrow or adipose tissue. UC-MSCs do not replace damaged cells; instead, they signal other cells to produce bioactive substances that reduce inflammation and promote cartilage repair. Data from emerging preclinical and clinical trials, which show significant improvements in WOMAC and VAS scores and a decrease in DAS28 with minimal adverse effects, suggest that UC-MSCs will improve pain and function and, in turn, overall quality of life. UC-MSCs represent a mechanistically distinct and clinically promising therapeutic effect for OA and RA, addressing both the inflammatory and degenerative condition of joint disease. However, there are still large, well-designed, standardized clinical trials that can best optimize doses and treatment plans. This narrative review summarizes the various forms of arthritis, disease pathogenesis, and preclinical and clinical evidence for the use of UC-MSCs in the treatment of arthritis, such as OA and RA.

metadata.title: A mechanically active microneedle platform integrated with engineered exosomes for enhanced tendon-bone regeneration.
metadata.abstract: Functional regeneration of the tendon-bone interface remains a major challenge because early healing is constrained by an adverse inflammatory microenvironment and insufficient mechanical cues. Here, we developed a mechano-regenerative strategy that combines YAP-primed engineered exosomes with localized biomaterial-based delivery and active mechanical stimulation. Exosomes derived from a YAP agonist (PY-60) preconditioned TDSCs (P-Exo) showed enhanced uptake and promoted the osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, accompanied by activation of YAP-associated signaling and PI3K-Akt-related pathways. To improve local retention, P-Exo were incorporated into a ROS-responsive adhesive hydrogel, which accelerated fibrocartilage formation, bone ingrowth, and biomechanical restoration in a rabbit tendon-bone healing model. To address more complex repair conditions, we engineered a three-layer self-contracting microneedle platform for deep-tissue delivery of P-Exo with concurrent active mechanical stimulation. In an infected rat rotator cuff model, this system reduced bacterial burden and oxidative stress, promoted a reparative macrophage polarization and angiogenesis, and improved tendon-bone structural regeneration, biomechanical strength, and functional recovery. Together, these findings support a therapeutic framework in which engineered exosome signaling and active mechanoregulation act in concert to enhance tendon-bone repair.

metadata.title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part II: Special Cases.
metadata.abstract: Aim: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can reveal subject-specific characteristics in patients with atypical CV dynamics. Methods: Seven special-case patients-including a heart transplant (HTx) recipient and individuals with bradycardia (low heart rate, HR), low dicrotic notch (DN), and intermittent arterial pulse waveform (APW) variations-were analyzed across three visits over the cardiac rehabilitation (CR) period. Radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) signals, acquired using micro-fabricated tactile sensors, were processed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework to extract multiple CV parameters. The analysis focused on descriptive characterization of subject-specific CV patterns in individual patients. Results: The patients exhibited highly heterogeneous CV profiles. Individuals with low HR exhibited relatively limited post-exercise HR changes. Individuals with low DN morphology exhibited elevated lower-order harmonic amplitudes. Individuals with intermittent APW variations exhibited cyclic changes in APW morphology at rest and during post-exercise recovery. Although CV patterns at rest differed across individuals, post-exercise assessment revealed more distinctive individual-specific differences, including differences between individuals within the same phenotype-based case subset. Across all patients and visits, RA measurements provided more stable and interpretable subject-specific CV patterns, whereas CA measurements were more susceptible to motion artifacts (MA) and sensor noise. For individuals with intermittent APW variations, the CA signals exhibited extremely poor signal quality, limiting their suitability for physiological interpretation. Conclusions: The SDOF-TF framework enabled the characterization of subject-specific, multi-parameter CV dynamics in these seven special cases. The findings illustrate the potential value of arterial pulse analysis for the individualized characterization of atypical CV dynamics. Future studies involving larger patient cohorts are needed to further investigate these findings and establish their clinical utility.

metadata.title: Post-Exercise Thermal Interventions and Nocturnal Sleep in Athletes: A Narrative Review of the Potential Underlying Physiological Mechanisms.
metadata.abstract: Sleep is essential for optimal performance and recovery in athletes. Post-exercise cold exposure, including cold water immersion and cryotherapy, is typically used to enhance recovery, but its effects on sleep remain unclear. Emerging evidence also suggests that post-exercise heat exposure, including sauna and hot water immersion before sleep may improve both objective and subjective sleep outcomes. However, the effectiveness of post-exercise thermal interventions for improving nocturnal sleep in athletes specifically has not yet been comprehensively evaluated. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence and discusses the potential physiological mechanisms by which post-exercise thermal interventions may influence nocturnal sleep in athletes. Despite methodological heterogeneity, existing research indicates that post-exercise thermal interventions may influence the subsequent nocturnal sleep of athletes through multiple and varying interacting mechanisms. For example, cold exposure close to bedtime (< 2 h) may disrupt sleep by reducing the distal-to-proximal skin temperature gradient (DPG), thereby increasing sleep onset latency and shortening sleep duration. In contrast, when applied more than 2 h before bedtime, cold exposure may improve sleep by augmenting parasympathetic tone and/or reducing muscle soreness and associated nocturnal movement. Although it remains unclear whether post-exercise heat exposure improves sleep via autonomic modulation or reduced muscle soreness, existing evidence indicates that sleep may be facilitated by an increased DPG. Moderating factors such as sex, time of day, environmental temperature, bedding microclimate, acclimatization status, and training load may influence the effects of post-exercise thermal interventions on sleep and should be investigated in future studies.

metadata.title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part I: General Cases.
metadata.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can capture subject-specific physiological characteristics and longitudinal changes in patients with diverse heart diseases. Method: Arterial pulse signals at the radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) of each patient were successfully recorded from all 18 patients using micro-fabricated tactile sensors. Signal quality was screened before analysis, and the accepted signals were analyzed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework. Key CV parameters, including time-based indices-heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), respiration rate (RR), and respiration modulation (RM), as well as harmonic amplitudes and normalized arterial pulse waveform (APW)-were extracted from measurements at rest and post-exercise across three rehabilitation visits in 18 patients with heterogeneous CV conditions. Longitudinal changes in CV parameters within subjects and variability between subjects were assessed. Results: Compared with a healthy reference, the patients exhibited heterogeneous CV profiles, with lower HRV in all patients except one with AF, who showed elevated HRV, and generally reduced post-exercise CV responses. Higher-order harmonic amplitudes were attenuated at the RA, while CA-derived APW measurements showed greater sensitivity to systolic upstroke slope. Marked inter-subject variability was evident in at-rest CV parameters and 5-min post-exercise responses. Longitudinal CV responses varied across rehabilitation visits, potentially reflecting multiple contributing factors. Conclusions: The 100% pulse acquisition rate supports the feasibility of the tactile sensor technology for pulse measurement, and the combined sensor technology and SDOF-TF framework enable quantitative characterization of shared and individualized CV patterns in cardiac patients and their post-exercise recovery, including time-based indices, harmonic signatures, site-specific differences, and interactions among CV parameters. These findings warrant further investigation in larger cohorts with appropriate physiological reference measurements.

metadata.title: The weight of the jersey: How athletic identity shapes the experience of Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome (FAIS) in Gaelic games.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome (FAIS) is a recognised source of hip pain in Gaelic games players. This study aimed to qualitatively explore the lived experiences of Gaelic games players with FAIS. METHODS: Twelve players (4 females;8 males) diagnosed with FAIS participated in semi-structured interviews. The Common-Sense model informed the interview schedule, addressing topics related to condition identity, causes, timeline, consequences and controllability. Reflexive thematic analysis was employed to inductively generate meaning from the data. RESULTS: One overarching theme, related to preserving athletic identity through injury, underpinned the three main themes: (1) Missed and dismissed opportunities for prevention and early intervention; (2) The quick fix or the long fight-Navigating the FAIS treatment dilemma capturing experiences with conservative and surgical treatment approaches; and (3) The weight of the jersey-The hidden burden of FAIS, exploring the impact of FAIS on players' emotional, psychological and social wellbeing. Across all themes, the complex interaction between the player and diverse stakeholders was central to shaping their experience of FAIS. CONCLUSION: This study provides novel insights into how players experience and navigate FAIS within an amateur, yet elite sporting environment. Understanding the importance of players' athletic identity is critical for developing strategies aimed at managing training load in young players, ensuring earlier diagnosis, establishing transparent care pathways and integrating psychosocial support into management plans. The influence of cultural and interpersonal factors on the players' experience of FAIS also plays a role in informing more holistic, athlete-centred approaches to the prevention and management of FAIS, within Gaelic games and similar sporting contexts.

metadata.title: Excessive COX-Prostaglandin Signaling Promotes Cellular Senescence and Impaired Skeletal Muscle Recovery in Aging.
metadata.abstract: The ability to recover skeletal muscle after periods of disuse declines with age leading to persistent deficits in strength and function that extend beyond muscle mass loss. Here, we investigated whether age-related alterations in lipid remodeling contribute to impairment in skeletal muscle recovery following disuse. Lipidomic and oxylipin profiling revealed that aged mouse muscle is characterized by sustained phosphatidylcholine and omega-6-dependent COX-prostaglandin signaling during early recovery from disuse atrophy. This persistent lipid mediator response was associated with increased senescence burden, fibrosis, and impaired functional recovery. Pharmacological suppression of COX signaling during reloading in aged mice reduced senescence markers, limited fibrosis, and improved muscle function independent of improved muscle size. Mechanistically, senescent induced macrophages produced COX-2-dependent PGE2 and impaired myotube size and fusion through paracrine signaling. Activation of EP2 signaling was sufficient to induce a senescent macrophage phenotype. Importantly, a similar age-associated dysregulation of oxylipin content was observed in older adults after limb immobilization, supporting the translational relevance of these findings. Together, our results identify sustained COX-prostaglandin signaling as a key feature of impaired skeletal muscle recovery with aging and suggest that targeted modulation of this pathway may improve muscle recovery in older individuals. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04416191.

metadata.title: Effects of Resveratrol Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage: A Narrative Review.
metadata.abstract: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) is a common consequence of high-intensity or unfamiliar physical activity and can lead to muscle soreness, inflammation, oxidative stress, and temporary loss of muscle function. Although various interventions have been explored to alleviate EIMD, resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic compound found in grapes, berries, and other plants, has attracted attention due to its potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This review aims to explore the effects of RES on EIMD in terms of its impact on muscle recovery, inflammation, and oxidative stress markers. This review synthesizes the results of preclinical and clinical studies and highlights the timing, dosage, and efficacy of exercise-associated RES. Although the results are promising, with several studies reporting reduced muscle damage and improved recovery, inconsistencies in RES administration timing, dosage, and bioavailability require further investigation. Understanding these factors is critical to optimizing the therapeutic potential of RES in both the exercise and clinical settings. Finally, the review summarizes the potential of RES as a safe and effective intervention for EIMD and implications for future research.

metadata.title: Arthroscopic Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Iliotibial Band Autograft With Bone Block.
metadata.abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction is the first-line treatment for ACL injury, whereas existing autologous grafts each have inherent limitations. This study describes the use of an iliotibial band (ITB) graft with a bone block for ACL reconstruction, designed as a femoral bone block combined with tibial tendon configuration, which precisely matches the anatomical attachment and biomechanical loading characteristics of the native ACL. The surgery is performed through arthroscopic evaluation, harvesting and weaving of the ITB with a bone block, creation of femoral and tibial bone tunnels, and graft introduction and fixation. This graft features the advantage of easy harvesting of the ITB, whereas the femoral bone column allows for rapid bone-to-bone healing, enhances stability within the femoral tunnel, and reduces the risk of tunnel widening and femoral-sided rerupture. Tibial-sided tendon fixation avoids excessive tibial tunnel enlargement and simplifies surgical steps. Arthroscopic ACL reconstruction using the ITB with bone block is technically straightforward and provides high initial stability. It offers another graft option for both primary treatment of ACL injury and revision surgery after failed reconstructions and is particularly suitable for patients with multiple previous tendon harvests from the same knee or those requiring large-diameter grafts because of bone tunnel enlargement.

metadata.title: Obturator internus muscle entrapment in posterior wall acetabular fractures: two cases with preoperative and intraoperative findings.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We report two cases of the rare presentation of obturator internus muscle (OI) entrapment in posterior wall fractures of the acetabulum. Although piriformis muscle entrapment has been previously reported, to the best of our knowledge, OI entrapment associated with posterior wall acetabular fractures has not been previously documented. CASE PRESENTATION: Case 1: A 38-year-old male presented with right hip and knee pain following a road traffic accident. He was diagnosed with a posterior hip dislocation, posterior wall and posterior column fractures of the acetabulum, and a posterior knee dislocation. During surgery, the OI muscle was found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. Case 2: A 43-year-old male sustained blunt abdominal trauma and a Pipkin type IV injury involving a femoral head fracture associated with a posterior wall acetabular fracture following a road traffic accident. After stabilisation of the abdominal injury with laparoscopic repair of the mesenteric injury, the patient underwent open reduction and internal fixation of the posterior wall fracture, along with removal of intra-articular fragments associated with an infra-foveal femoral head fracture. Intraoperatively, the OI muscle was similarly found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. In both cases, retrospective review of the preoperative CT images demonstrated OI interposition corresponding to the intraoperative findings. Both patients followed a standard postoperative rehabilitation protocol. At the one-year follow-up, both patients had satisfactory clinical outcomes, with Merle d'Aubigné-Postel scores of 16 and 17 and Harris Hip Scores of 92.7 and 93 for Cases 1 and 2, respectively. Neither patient showed radiographic evidence of post-traumatic arthritis. CONCLUSION: These cases highlight the importance of recognising OI muscle entrapment as a potential cause of difficulty in reducing posterior wall acetabular fractures. Careful evaluation of preoperative CT images, particularly using soft-tissue window settings, may facilitate the identification of OI interposition. Intraoperatively, failure to identify the OI tendon between the superior and inferior gemelli, when both are clearly identified, should raise suspicion of entrapment. Meticulous identification of soft-tissue structures may help achieve anatomical fracture reduction and successful fixation.

metadata.title: Immediate effect of verbal cues on ACL injury relevant Knee loading during 180° and 90° cutting maneuvers in female university soccer and basketball athletes.
metadata.abstract: Young female athletes possess a high risk of rupturing their anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). High external peak knee abduction moments (pKAM) are a likely key risk factor for non-contact ACL injuries. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of performance-based movement feedback on pKAM during cutting maneuvers in female university athletes. Thirty-four female university soccer and basketball athletes completed preplanned 180° and 90° cutting trials while ground reaction forces and kinematics were simultaneously captured. Participants immediately received verbal cues targeting foot strike angle, foot progression angle, or trunk lean angle based on their performance. Athletes then repeated the trials post-feedback. Changes in pKAM between baseline and post-feedback trials were analyzed. Soccer and basketball athletes who received the FOOTstrike-angle cue significantly reduced pKAM for both cutting tasks (Soccer: 180°; -0.21 Nm/kg, p < 0.01, d = 0.92; 90°; -0.28 Nm/kg, p < 0.01, d = 1.16. Basketball: 180°; -0.07 Nm/kg, p = 0.02, d = 0.76; 90°; -0.30 Nm/kg, p < 0.01, d = 0.82). The FOOTpro-angle cue significantly reduced pKAM during the 180° cut for soccer athletes (-0.10 Nm/kg, p = 0.01, d = 0.60), but not basketball. The TRUNKlean cue did not significantly affect pKAM for either sport. Individual feedback targeting forefoot landings and neutral foot progression angles can elicit immediate technique change and reduce ACL injury relevant knee loading during cutting maneuvers.

metadata.title: From bouts to readiness to compete: temporal dynamics of stress, fatigue, recovery and monitoring-informed decisions in combat sports.
metadata.abstract: Combat-sport tournaments require decisions before responses to previous efforts have resolved. Detecting a change does not establish that an indicator predicts the next task or improves a decision. This Perspective proposes a task- and time-specific framework linking prior bouts, recovery time and subsequent demands through three evidentiary requirements. Responsiveness concerns reproducible changes beyond measurement error when an indicator represents a response to effort. Predictive validity concerns anticipation of a pre-specified subsequent outcome and added information beyond simpler measures. Decision utility concerns improved outcomes relative to usual practice. Indicators interpreted as current status or stable capacity need not respond to prior effort, but still require adequate measurement properties and prospective evaluation. Evidence from repeated bouts, recovery interventions, mental fatigue, sleep restriction and weight loss suggests that monitoring domains are not interchangeable. The framework retains discordant indicators, evaluates combinations and communicates uncertainty without global clearance labels. Three hypotheses address task and time dependence, maintained performance with increasing effort cost, and indicator-informed decisions. Medical decisions remain independent and take precedence. This is an operational extension of existing principles, not a validated predictive tool.

metadata.title: Case Study Insights Into Female World-Class and Elite Athletes' Training and Physiology.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: This article offers a structured overview of published case studies involving elite and world-class female Olympic athletes, highlighting the unique insights these studies provide into training characteristics, physiology, performance, and female-specific factors. METHODS: Four databases were systematically searched for peer-reviewed case studies involving tiers 4 to 5 female Olympic athletes reporting individual-level data on training, physiological, and/or performance characteristics. RESULTS: Thirty-eight studies describing 54 elite and world-class female athletes from 18 countries and 19 Olympic sports met the inclusion criteria. Most studies were published after 2017 (68%), originated from Europe (58%), and involved endurance sports (81%). Fifteen studies examined long-term athlete development, with observation periods ranging from 4 to 26 years. Fourteen studies reported annual training and physiological characteristics across 10 sports including training volume, intensity distribution, periodization, and physiological profiling. Four studies examined altitude training, 8 addressed competition demands, tapering, and precompetition strategies, and 8 focused on female-specific physiology, health, and performance, including energy availability, menstrual function, hormonal cycle monitoring and pregnancy, and postpartum return to sport. CONCLUSION: Case studies provide unique athlete-centered insights into the complex interactions between training, physiology, health, and performance in elite female athletes. Collectively, they demonstrate that pathways to world-class performance are highly individualized, while generating hypotheses that complement group-based research. Future case studies should prioritize underrepresented sports, geographical regions, and female-specific topics to expand the diversity of performance environments and athlete populations represented in the literature.

metadata.title: "Why wouldn't you?": the co-design and feasibility of a neck exercise training programme (NExT-TaCKLE) to reduce head acceleration events in men's academy rugby league.
metadata.abstract: This qualitative study aimed to co-design and explore the feasibility, barriers and facilitators of a neck-exercise training intervention aiming to reduce head acceleration events (HAEs) in men's academy rugby league. A steering group of researchers and practitioners from five academy rugby league teams co-designed a neck-training programme (Neck Exercise Training - Tackle and Contact Kinematics, Load, Exposure (NExT-TaCKLE) programme). The NExT-TaCKLE programme was designed to give performance and medical practitioners exercises catering to different equipment availability; target neck musculature across flexion, extension, bilateral flexion and rotation; and progress from movement competency to perturbation-focused training blocks. The NExT-TacCKLE programme was trialled for a 6-week period in three teams. Semistructured interviews were completed with a practitioner and player from each team to determine the feasibility of NExT-TacCKLE, including barriers and facilitators to implementation. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to analyse the interview data and generate themes. Data were then revisited and mapped to feasibility areas of interest and the capability, opportunity and motivation model for behaviour change. Eight themes were generated during the reflexive thematic analysis. The programme showed good acceptability and demand; however, the implementation, integration and practicality were feasibility areas where the programme could be improved. Key barriers (eg, equipment, coach-to-athlete ratio, practitioner experience) and facilitators (eg, belief in the intervention effectiveness, perceived simple integration into existing setups) were identified. Working with practitioners, the NExT-TaCKLE programme was developed for implementation with academy rugby league players. This study can help inform future development of the NExT-TaCKLE and other neck-training programmes, as well as other injury prevention and implementation strategies. Future research is needed to evaluate the effectiveness of the programme to reduce HAEs.

metadata.title: Integrated Decision-Making Under Uncertainty in High-Performance Sport Support Systems.
metadata.abstract: Greater expertise, more data, and increased collaboration do not necessarily improve decisions in high-performance sport. Support systems must connect evidence and professional judgement to action under time pressure, uncertainty, and competing priorities. This narrative review draws on targeted database and citation searches to synthesize literature on performance support, team functioning, leadership, sport science, and decision science. The proposed framework combines established decision principles with qualitative triage and selective integration. Urgency, uncertainty, risk and consequences, reversibility, interdisciplinary interdependence, and stakeholder differences guide the choice between discipline-led decisions, consultation or coordinated input, and integrated decision-making. Five interdependent functions organize integrated work: framing the problem and decision; identifying contributors and governance; interpreting information and generating options; committing to and communicating a course of action; and acting, monitoring, and learning. Governance distinguishes information provision, recommendations, final authority, and implementation responsibility, with referral or escalation available from any working mode. Athlete values and decision rights shape the process, including shared decision-making and consent where required. Coaches help translate recommendations into feasible training and competition plans. Scientific reasoning, applied inquiry, innovation, and integrative leadership support these functions. Hypothetical examples address return to sport, training modification, and technology adoption. The framework remains conceptual, and evaluation should examine content validity, usability, triage consistency, implementation burden, and decision processes before assessing health and performance effects. Decision quality should be judged against the information and uncertainty present when decisions were made.
